messages:
elaine: Heads-up — BigCorp asked for a 6mo pin exemption on model-x-v2 citing regulatory audit timelines. they want a firm migration incentive (credit or SLA) if we require cutover earlier. can we propose a framework?
samir: Can you paste their exact ask? do they want the pin on hosted only or across Dedicated/Private too?
elaine: Hosted + Dedicated. quote: "need stability for Q3 audit window; will not migrate unless incentives included". CC @maria for customer fidelity context.
maria: Yep — they’re on Dedicated, heavy embed usage. main ask is timeline certainty and a documented rollback plan. they’re sensitive to perf regressions.
jordan: Technical constraints: model-x-v2 uses a custom kv-cache layout we rely on. keeping it long-term increases maintenance cost and blocks some runtime optimizations.
kevin: If we extend pin windows by 6mo we need to keep a compatibility shim for next-gen kernels. That adds ~1.5 engineer-months to infra+runtime upkeep per quarter.
sophia: On eval side, we need to lock benchmark sets for pinned variants. propose a gated eval every 30 days: run quality regression suite + embed drift checks. fail -> freeze new feature pushes to that variant.
samir: Ok — quick proposal sketch:
- Pin Exception Length: 6 months (customer-requested)
- Incentive options: (A) 3 months free Dedicated credits, (B) SLO bump for pin window, (C) engineering support SLA (paid)
- Acceptance criteria for pin grant: must pass monthly regression gates, agree to migration prep checklist, and allow telemetry access for perf audits.
- Sunset plan: 90d notice + canary migration window.

jordan: Additions from eng:
- Compatibility shim supported only on pinned branch (no forward-port guarantee)
- Canaries: run 1% traffic on hosted, up to 10% on Dedicated liters for 2 weeks.
- Rollback hooks + automatic fallback to model-x-v1 if latency > p95 threshold.

elaine: We should capture cost economics in the proposal. kevin, can you estimate infra delta for shim + canary traffic?
kevin: Rough numbers:
- Shim maintenance: ~0.375 FTE ongoing -> monthly ~$6.5k in cost allocation
- Canary + dual-serving overhead: +8% token cost for the duration of rollout
- One-time migration assist: ~40 engineering hours if we do active hand-holding

maria: From CS POV, customers care about: 1) no surprise changes, 2) migration runway, 3) credits help with buy-in. they'd take (A) or a mix of A+C.
sophia: Metric gating specifics I propose:
- Quality: eval-suite pass rate >= 98% (weighted by critical intents)
- Embedding drift: cosine similarity median >= 0.95 vs baseline
- Perf: p95 latency delta <= +20ms, token cost delta <= +10%
- If any gate fails twice in a row -> revoke new pin grants and start migration assistance.

samir: Sounds reasonable. Need legal + finance input on credits and SLA language. Also product needs a formal migration incentive template.
elaine: Drafting a customer-facing one-pager. rough outline:
- Summary of pin exception
- Incentives offered (A/B/C) with exact amounts
- Monitoring & gating clauses
- Migration playbook & timelines
- Billing implications

jordan: For the migration playbook include the command snippets we use for canary rollout and rollback. e.g.:
```
# canary route
redwood route set --model model-x-v3 --percent 1 --region us-west
# rollback
redwood route set --model model-x-v1 --percent 100
```

maria: Also include escalation contacts and an opt-in form for customers to pick incentives.

product-bot: Reminder — any pin-exception >90 days requires exec approval per policy POL-ONBOARD-3.

samir: Good catch. we'll route to ops-review and legal. propose timeline:
- Draft proposal -> internal review (3 business days)
- Customer review & selection of incentives (7 business days)
- Implement shim + agree telemetry (2 weeks)
- Start canary + gated ramp (2–4 weeks)

elaine: I'll assemble proposal doc and post it here. action items:
- elaine: draft customer one-pager + template (due in 48h)
- kevin: cost estimate + billing language (48h)
- sophia: regression gate config + eval run script (72h)
- jordan: canary + rollback command snippets + runtime constraints (48h)
- maria: customer negotiation playbook + opt-in form draft (72h)

maria: quick Q — do we allow stacked pins? e.g., multiple exceptions for same tenant across models? that complicates infra.
jordan: We should avoid stacked long-term pins unless exec-approved. add to policy.
samir: I'll add a line to the proposal: "stacked exceptions disallowed without exec sign-off".

elaine: Thanks team. posting draft later today. :sparkles:
